📰 General

Airman Killed in Iraqi Refueling Tanker Crash; Kentucky Native Identified •

Tech. Sgt. Ashley B. Pruitt, a 34-year-old airman from Bardstown, Kentucky, was identified as one of six U.S. airmen aboard a refueling tanker that crashed in Iraq on Friday. The crash occurred during a mission supporting Operation Inherent Resolve. Initial reports indicate the plane went down near Al Asim Airbase in Iraq. Investigations into the cause of the crash are currently underway.

🌍 World

Iran’s Actions in Strait of Hormuz Raise Serious Legal and Operational Concerns •

Recent attacks by Iran on commercial vessels within the Strait of Hormuz represent a violation of international maritime law. These actions, including the potential deployment of mines, contravene both the law of the sea and the law of armed conflict. The narrow waterway’s strategic importance as a global oil transit route makes enforcement of these rules exceptionally challenging. International observers are highlighting the practical difficulties in holding Iran accountable for these escalating provocations.

🦅 US

Bomb Cyclone Unleashes Record Snowfall, Threatening Midwest and Great Lakes •

A rapidly intensifying bomb cyclone is bringing historic snowfall to the Midwest and Great Lakes regions. The storm is dumping multiple feet of snow, creating blizzard conditions and significant travel disruptions. Extreme wind gusts are compounding the hazardous weather, leading to whiteout conditions in some areas. National Weather Service warnings remain in effect for numerous states as forecasters continue to monitor the storm’s intensity and potential impacts.

💰 Business

F-35 Software Upgrades Significantly Delayed, Pentagon Report Reveals •

A recent Pentagon report suggests substantial delays in the delivery of major software upgrades for the F-35 Lightning II fighter jet. The delays are attributed to challenges integrating new software versions with existing systems. Lockheed Martin, the primary contractor for the F-35, is facing difficulties in meeting the planned timelines for these critical updates. The report highlights concerns about potential impacts on the program’s operational readiness and future capabilities. Further investigation into the root causes of the delays is reportedly underway.

💻 Technology

New Japanese Games Hit Release: Crimson Desert, RUSHING BEAT X, and More! •

This week saw several notable Japanese video game releases, with Crimson Desert launching for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. RUSHING BEAT X: Return of Brawl Brothers was also released, targeting PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. The releases include titles available across multiple platforms, catering to a wide range of gaming preferences. These new games represent a diverse selection of titles debuting in the Japanese market.

🎭 Entertainment

Harry Styles Delivers Memorable Sketches on Saturday Night Live Season 51 •

Harry Styles hosted Saturday Night Live’s 51st season, marking his debut on the show. During his appearance, Styles performed several sketches, including a musical number promoting his album, Kiss Me, Honestly. The episode also featured a segment on Brittany Broski’s podcast, highlighting Styles’ recent promotional activities. The broadcast followed Styles’ busy month, which included appearances at the BRIT Awards and a Netflix taping for Kiss Me, Honestly.

🏅 Sports

Ohio State Secures NCAA Tournament Berth, Faces TCU in First Round •

The Ohio State men’s basketball team earned an at-large invitation to the 2026 NCAA Tournament, receiving the eighth seed. They will compete against the ninth-seeded Texas Christian Horned Frogs in the first round of the tournament. A victory for the Buckeyes would likely set up a second-round matchup against the number one seeded Duke Blue Devils. This marks the program’s first NCAA Tournament appearance in four years. The game is scheduled for [Date - omitted from provided text].

🔬 Science

140-Foot Asteroid 2007 EG Zips Past Earth, NASA Reports Safe Encounter •

A 140-foot asteroid, designated 2007 EG, approached Earth overnight at a speed of approximately 17,000 miles per hour. NASA issued an alert regarding the close proximity of the space rock, which was tracked by astronomers globally. The asteroid’s trajectory posed no immediate threat to Earth, and it is now moving further away. Scientists continue to monitor near-Earth objects for potential future approaches.

🩺 Health

Vitamin D Supplementation Shows Promise in Reducing Long COVID Symptoms •

A new study conducted by Mass General Brigham investigated the potential link between vitamin D supplementation and the persistence of long COVID symptoms. Researchers analyzed data from a large group of individuals experiencing lingering symptoms following a COVID-19 infection. The study suggests that high doses of vitamin D may be associated with a reduced risk of developing persistent long COVID symptoms. Further research is needed to confirm these findings and determine the optimal dosage for individuals seeking relief.
